newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent diesel surges on NYMEX gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent diesel surges on NYMEX gains.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel prices surged as NYMEX heating oil futures set a new contract high in early after-hours trade on Thursday, traders said.

Chicago differentials firmed on talk of an outage at Mobil Corp's 188,000 barrel per day Joliet, Ill., refinery, and sightings of Mobil in the market for spot unleaded gasoline and diesel fuel barrels.
A Mobil refinery spokeswoman declined comment on the operational status of the refinery. "It's not our policy to speak about operating situations," she said.
Outages at several key refineries in the region was keeping diesel differentials steady in the wake of the week-long rally in front-month heating oil futures, traders said.
Group Three low sulphur diesel was talked even to 0.25 cent over the print for prompt deliveries and 0.25 cent under to even with the print for later deliveries.
Chicago prompt low sulphur diesel remained 0.75/0.50 cent under the print for all October timings.
High sulphur diesel remained 2.50 cents under the print in Chicago and 1.25/1.50 cents under the print in Group Three.
Group Three unleaded was steady at 1.25/1.0 cent under the print for prompt deliveries and 1.50/1.25 cent under for later deliveries, with premium 2.50 cents higher.
Chicago prompt October unleaded differentials remained 0.75/0.50 cent under the print, with later deliveries talked 1.75/1.50 cent under and premium three cents higher, traders said.
Jet/kero was unchanged at 1.50/1.75 cents over the print in Chicago and 1.25/1.50 cents over the print in Group Three.
